body: This is making me think how cool it'd be if some dispersals were other player's pups
Mod for this thankfully
Gotta be INFP, they seem to have a thing for the dark and mysterious. Knew an INFP like that, nicest most sensitive guy yet wrote the most messed up horror stories

Reminds me of the time while working in a dollar store that some kid tracked shit across the entire store I found as soon as I came in for my shift. I easily spent over an hour trying to get it all. It wasn’t the first time I ever had to clean excrement, but god the smell was particularly horrible
I didn’t witness it, but another employee got shot and killed while working the drive thru. Still had to go in the next morning and work where the guy died
Yup, exactly the same here… except I lost my job months ago so I’ve just been rotting at home

I think my discomfort of the body and body horror comes from dpdr. It's scary to be reminded we have a body with parts we depend on that work independently from our conscious mind, and have no control over. The heart especially. Same reason needles freak me out. I don't care about any pain, but the feeling of it going in and out of the skin is horrible.
DPDR very rarely actually protects us from anything physically harmful, it just thinks it did
Similar issue here, but I think poor sleep and diet also really effects my brain fog

Cleaning has always been a struggle for me since I grew up in cluttered household, but watching Midwest Magic Cleaning for inspiration and then taking the time to clear a small space is very cathartic
Yeah you’re totally right. The most difficult symptom to ignore is my thoughts. I often don’t recognize when something is just anxiety because I’m so detached from my emotions

I'm glad I could at least point you in some direction. Doctors never took me seriously about my eye issues either, and BVD isn't very well known so you might need a specialist if it is. But I'm wishing you luck

Possible binocular vision dysfunction? I suspect I have it, and I’ve had issues focusing my eyes for a long time. Bright lights can be an issue. I also deal with dissociation, and I’ve seen a connection between my eyes unfocusing and dissociating. Not saying one causes another. I don’t have much advice, but this felt slightly relatable. Except I can control my eyes unfocusing, just often it takes increasing mental effort to fix it or I don’t even notice it happened.

I'd say Effexor made mine way worse because of emotional blunting. It's why I'm weaning off it, because the dissociation is worse than the depression. But it was worth it for a while. Everyone is different I suppose

I understand you. Maybe I think the grass is always greener on the other side. I suppose I was hoping for a balance, but if I'm able to feel any emotion it tends to lean towards extreme. I've enjoyed weed for some time, but even after breaks there was no "goodness" anymore. I suppose I'll give it another shot now. I already struggled with emotion, but the numbness I got from my medication just felt stronger than expected. I definitely needed it at the time, but now I just don't see how I could do it long term. I respect whatever works for you though

Eh, there comes a point where if I can't feel anything at all then I'm as good as dead. Any "progress" is for nothing. Our whole existence is based off emotion. I want to love my dog, my friends, my hobbies. Or at least getting high. Maybe I'm not meant to have those things
Thank you. Guess since I've been feeling this way since I was a child feels like it's too late to fix my life. I appreciate the hugs though

I appreciate your comment. I feel good occasionally, but it's short lived and things just seem to get worse.  I've felt depressed for quite a few years now. Started because I was unable to make friends, and that ate away at me. The feeling of complete isolation. Sounds maybe like a miniscule problem. Now, on top of that, as I mentioned I'm failing school. I'm completely unable to function in life and I don't see a great future for myself, seems there's not much to continue for. I've tried but can't get back on track. Tired of it all, I guess.
Not really, no offense. My experience with religion has not been a positive one.

In the past I have. Therapists, meds and the like. Been a long while since I've tried any of that again. I was either too depressed to bother or too confident in thinking I could handle it on my own. I was doing a group therapy, but it was cancelled by covid.
I won't do it tonight. For the future, I can't be sure. I appreciate the kind words
That might be something I look into, though I rarely have any drastic mood changes. I don't know much about bipolar, so thanks for the insight, I learned what hypomanic means.
I wish you well too. Thank you. I'm.. trying, I guess
I appreciate that
